title: Commanders punter Tress Way ‘pretty sure’ this season will be his last
content:
Tress Way, the Commanders’ three-time Pro Bowl punter and longest-tenured player, said Thursday that he is “pretty sure” this will be his last season in the NFL.

“I thought about it a long time. It has been so special for me playing here because I was an undrafted free agent, cut by the Bears, bounced around, sleeping on the couch and doing workouts,” Way said Thursday afternoon, before choking up. “I got picked up by the Bears again, (cut) by the Bears again. And then when I got picked up here on the waiver wire — for all the fantasy folks out there, I was a waiver wire claim — when I got claimed on the waver wire, dude, I just felt wanted here. I’ve felt wanted here my whole career, so I didn’t want to play anywhere else.”

Washington claimed Way in 2014 and he quickly won the starting job, grossing an NFL-best 47.5 yards per punt in his first season. In 2019, he was voted a second-team All-Pro and selected to his first of three career Pro Bowls with an NFL-high 49.6 yards per punt. He also kicked the longest punt in the league that season, 79 yards, in a win over the Carolina Panthers.

But perhaps the signature play of his career was not a punt, but a pass completion: In the 2024 NFC Championship game against the Eagles, the Commanders audibled to fake a punt and Way found tight end Ben Sinnott for a 23-year completion.

“I can still go back to being in the moment whenever Reavo (safety/punt protector Jeremy Reaves) made the audible on the field,” Way, 36, recalled. “Things weren’t going our way out the gate, my family and friends are in the stands in the NFC Championship. We’re one game away from the Super Bowl and it’s like, ‘I’m gonna throw a freaking pass right now.’”

Way long ago set the franchise record for most punting yards, which now stands at 39,031. With at least 65 punts this season he would top Mike Bragg (896) for the most in team history. He also has a chance to pass Art Monk (205) for the third-most career games played by a Washington player.

Way has the rare distinction of being an NFL punter who is also one of the team’s most popular players, beloved by players, coaches and fans. Throughout his 12 seasons, he’s played for two team owners and four head coaches (including interim Bill Callahan in 2019), held for 12 kickers and seen 16 starting quarterbacks come through Washington.

“I had heard a few times before that this could possibly be the last one,” Reaves said when asked about his initial reaction to Way’s likely impending retirement. “Fifty precent of me didn’t want to believe (it) and 50 percent of me felt like it was real this time. It was a gut punch. Sucked. … That’s my brother.”

Way and Reaves became especially close in their years together, with the latter often crediting Way for helping him make the Commanders’ active roster after years of bouncing on and off the practice squad. Way helped former coach Ron Rivera surprise Reaves with the news of his Pro Bowl selection in 2022, then four years later officiated his wedding.

“Every big moment of my life he’s been a part of,” Reaves said Thursday, as the tears started to roll.

Reaves (defense) and Way (special teams) were both voted as a season-long captains this season.

“Send him off on a high note,” Reaves said. “Send him off the right way.”
